active_paradigms.idea: Replace the cost-only beam with duplicate-aware best-first beam search over canonical stack states
active_paradigms.description: The current initializer expands one destination decision per required removal, but ranks beam nodes almost entirely by energy already paid; this systematically discards states that pay a little more now to expose a long sequence of small labels later. Use std::priority_queue for a best-first/beam-frontier search and std::unordered_map keyed by a compact canonical representation of the remaining stacks, retaining only the lowest energy reaching each equivalent state. Score each frontier state by g plus an admissible-or-at-least-strong lower-bound estimate: count current blockers above each soon-required label, discount overlaps, and heavily reward immediately removable consecutive labels. Expand only the best few destinations according to a destination score based on the earliest label buried by the inserted block, rather than expanding all nine destinations uniformly. Canonicalize empty stack identities and, where safe, interchangeable stacks to eliminate many duplicate states. Keep a diverse frontier by retaining several states from distinct signatures, such as the vector of locations/heights of the next 20 labels, instead of selecting the global lowest g states only. This directly improves the initial basin delivered to subsequent local search and should be much more useful than the current comparator's sum-of-top-labels tie break.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce total energy V, hence raise the actual mean absolute score 10000-V; operation count is naturally far below 5000 under this move model.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not canonicalize nonempty stacks merely by sorting them: stack order is semantically essential. The transposition key must include every remaining stack sequence and the next required label. A heuristic used for ordering need not be admissible if this remains a heuristic beam, but never use it to claim exact pruning. Reserve enough time for the improvement phase because current state copying and full-vector keys can consume the 2 second limit.

active_paradigms.idea: Use ruin-and-recreate large-neighborhood search that reoptimizes a contiguous suffix by rollout trials
active_paradigms.description: The present SA mutates destination genes but evaluates each mutation against a fixed policy representation; it mostly makes random one-gene or short-block changes and repeatedly reconstructs prefixes, so it struggles to cross coordinated destination changes. Use std::discrete_distribution to select a difficult interval, biased toward labels whose extraction currently moves many boxes or whose moved block contains near-future labels. Preserve the exact simulated prefix before that interval, erase the destination decisions for a sizeable suffix/window, and regenerate them jointly with many randomized greedy rollouts. In each rollout, choose among the top few destinations using a stochastic score that estimates both the immediate block size and how many of the next W labels become blocked by the placement. Select the best complete repaired plan by exact simulation, accept improvements always, and occasionally accept a bounded deterioration early in the time budget. Include neighborhoods that extend to the end of the instance, since a destination choice at an early label can alter all later stack membership. This is fundamentally stronger than coordinate descent because a set of individually bad changes can be accepted together when it exposes a better global arrangement.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the local minima of single-coordinate destination assignment and lower the number and size of future blocker transfers, which dominate V.
active_paradigms.cautions: The prefix must be replayed exactly under the retained decisions before generating a repair; using positions from the old suffix after any changed decision is invalid. Always exact-simulate a candidate before retaining it, including correction of a destination equal to the source. Make rollout count adaptive to remaining time and favor moderate windows (for example 10-50 targets) plus occasional suffix-wide ruins; overly large random repairs will merely recreate weak initial solutions.

active_paradigms.idea: Extend the solution space with bounded proactive split moves and search them by Monte-Carlo tree selection
active_paradigms.description: The current program imposes a strong restriction: immediately before removing label k it moves the entire blocker suffix once, then removes k. That is feasible but not necessarily optimal, because proactively moving only a top sub-block can preserve a useful lower block, make an empty buffer available, or avoid placing an important near-future label beneath a large unrelated suffix. Use std::mt19937 to run a bounded Monte-Carlo tree search at selected high-cost decision states. A tree action should include the existing full-block extraction action plus a small set of proactive legal cuts: move the top q boxes of the current stack, or move the suffix starting at a strategically selected one of the next W labels, to a candidate destination. Rollouts then follow a fast deterministic greedy extractor until a horizon or completion, and backpropagate negative exact energy plus a lower-bound terminal estimate. Restrict proactive actions to a short candidate list derived from local minima/next-label positions, so branching stays manageable. Commit only an action sequence whose full simulation improves the incumbent, then continue normal extraction and invoke the search again when the next forced block is large. This tests a qualitatively larger legal-operation space that the current gene representation cannot express at all.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Find reductions in energy unavailable to the one-forced-move-per-label policy, especially rare configurations where splitting/repositioning a blocker block prevents repeated large transfers later.
active_paradigms.cautions: Every proactive move costs moved_count+1, so unrestricted MCTS will waste energy; impose a strict depth/action budget and require a rollout advantage over the direct forced move. The output simulator must support arbitrary legal op1 moves and update all box positions correctly, rather than assuming that every op1 begins immediately above the current target. Keep a final deterministic legality replay and enforce the 5000-operation cap; discard any exploratory sequence that cannot be completed safely.
